query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these incident tickets.

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Provides a clean categorical axis derived from short_description, enabling grouping and volume analysis. Sample values (database_access, vpn_connectivity, network_connectivity, software_issue) are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: service_domain
per_column.rationale: A higher-level rollup of incident_category; adds a coarser grouping axis but is largely derivable from and redundant with incident_category. Values are well grounded in the description text.

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: The table already contains assigned_to and closed_by, making this largely redundant. More critically, source_text samples show no person names, yet specific technicians are confidently produced per row; unless copied from an existing column, these values are not grounded in the shown evidence.

per_column.name: self_assigned_resolution
per_column.rationale: Comparing whether the assignee resolved their own ticket could be a useful axis, but it requires assigned_to vs closed_by which aren't in the shown source samples. The provided evidence (only description/timestamps) does not support the true/false assertions, suggesting unwarranted specificity.

per_column.name: recurring_incident_pattern
per_column.rationale: Potentially useful for spotting repeat problems, but the value is 'true' for 469/500 rows (near-constant), sharply limiting analytical leverage. Rows like 'Unable to access the database' are flagged recurring with no textual support for recurrence, indicating largely inferred/invented values.

judge.rationale: The categorical columns (incident_category, service_domain) are the strongest: well-grounded in short_description and offering real grouping axes, though the second is somewhat redundant with the first. The remaining three are weaker: assigned_technician duplicates existing assigned_to/closed_by fields, and self_assigned_resolution and recurring_incident_pattern assert row-level facts (specific names, recurrence flags) not supported by the shown source text, with recurring_incident_pattern also near-constant. Overall the set provides moderate analytical value but carries notable groundedness concerns from confidently produced values the evidence does not substantiate.
